goodbye.note: Casual: Baai! To someone who is leaving: Mooi loop! (go well).

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: Baie dankie.

youre_welcome.note: Also common: Dis 'n plesier, or Nie te danke nie.

no.note: Sounds like 'near' without the r. 'Not' is nie.

sorry.note: Full form: Ek is jammer. Sorry is also used a lot.

excuse_me.note: Also very common: Ekskuus! or Ekskuus tog!

good_morning.note: Casual: Môre! The ô sounds like the 'aw' in 'law'.

how_are_you.note: U is the polite 'you'. Casual: Hoe gaan dit? or Hoe gaan dit met jou?

im_fine.note: Shorter: Goed, dankie. To ask back: En met u?

im_from.note: Also common: Ek kom uit … or Ek is van …

speak_english.note: Casual: Praat jy Engels? Most Afrikaans speakers also speak English.

dont_understand.note: Longer sentences take a double nie: Ek verstaan nie wat u sê nie.

speak_slowly.note: Softer: Kan u asseblief stadiger praat?

where.note: The w is said like v: 'vaar'. Where to? Waarheen?

what.note: Wat? alone can sound blunt; to ask someone to repeat, say Ekskuus? or Sorry?

when.note: Stress on the second part: va-NEER.

who.note: Sounds like 'vee'. Whose? is Wie s'n?

how_much.note: Also very common: Wat kos dit?

where_bathroom.note: In someone's home, ask for die badkamer (the bathroom).

one.note: Sounds like 'ee-un'. Not the same as 'n (a, an), which is said like a short 'uh'.

three.note: Sounds like 'dree', with a rolled r.

four.note: The v is an f sound: 'feer'.

five.note: The y sounds like the 'ay' in 'say': 'fayf'.

seven.note: The w is a v sound: 'SEE-uh-vuh'.

eight.note: The g is throaty, like the ch in Scottish 'loch'.

water.note: Said 'VAH-tuhr': the w is a v sound and the r is pronounced. Tap water: kraanwater.

tea.note: Rooibostee (rooibos tea) is a South African favourite.

bread.note: A bread roll is a broodjie.

im_hungry.note: In speech often: Ek's honger. Very hungry: Ek is baie honger.

menu_please.note: Many people also say die menu. Politer: Kan ek die spyskaart kry, asseblief?

bill_please.note: Politer: Kan ek die rekening kry, asseblief?

delicious.note: Everyday favourite: Lekker! It works for food, weather and good times.

no_meat.note: Note the double nie. Also: Ek is 'n vegetariër.

right.note: Turn right: Draai regs. 'Correct' is reg, without the s.

straight_ahead.note: Keep going straight: Gaan reguit aan.

stop_here.note: Also common: Hou asseblief hier stil.

want_to_go.note: Very common in speech: Ek wil … toe gaan.

is_it_far.note: Is it a long walk? Is dit ver om te loop?

too_expensive.note: In speech usually: Dis te duur.

id_like_this.text: Ek wil graag hierdie een hê, asseblief
id_like_this.note: Also common: Ek sal hierdie een vat (I'll take this one).

just_looking.note: Also: Ek kyk maar net rond.

cash.note: To pay in cash: kontant betaal.

closed.note: Sounds like 'too'. Formal signs may say Gesluit.

yesterday.note: The g is throaty, like the ch in Scottish 'loch'.

now.note: Careful: nou-nou means 'in a little while'. Right now: nou dadelik.

later.note: Said 'LAH-tuhr', with the r pronounced. Also very common: netnou (in a while).

good_night.note: Casual: Nag! When going to bed: Lekker slaap!

see_you_later.note: Also: Tot later! or just Sien jou!

wait_moment.note: Also: Net 'n oomblik, asseblief. Casual: Wag gou!

call_police.note: In South Africa the police emergency number is 10111.

dont_feel_well.note: Lekker here means 'well'. Also: Ek is siek (I'm ill).

allergic.note: Example: Ek is allergies vir neute (nuts).

no_problem.note: The final nie is the Afrikaans double negative. Casual: Dis reg! (That's fine).

dont_know.note: Also: Ek het geen idee nie (I have no idea).

i_like_it.note: For food or something you enjoy: Dis lekker!

im_happy.note: Glad or pleased right now: Ek is bly.

congratulations.note: On a birthday: Veels geluk met jou verjaarsdag!
